name: Bahamas
prevalence_note: Central Bank of The Bahamas (CBOB) & Royal Bahamas Police Force (RBPF) 2025-2026: bank-detail update phishing/vishing, AI deepfake celebrity/official investment calls, upfront-fee consumer loan & fake job advertisements, and cash-prize advance-fee scams dominate.
cross_border_note: Uses +1-242 within NANP; scammers spoof US (+1) and +1-242 numbers on voice calls and WhatsApp while misusing Bahamian public figures in deepfake promos.

scams.name: RBPF-Warned Bank Account Update Phishing & OTP Vishing Call
scams.name_en: Fake Bahamian bank notification or call prompting urgent account detail update and OTP disclosure
scams.signals_en: Unsolicited SMS, WhatsApp, or phone call claiming a Bahamian bank account or POS card needs urgent verification via a link or reading out confidential login/OTP codes.
scams.legit_en: RBPF advises citizens never to click unknown banking links and to verify any account update request directly at a local branch or official bank number.
bait_tactics: Tell the caller you live five minutes from the Nassau branch and will walk in with your ID instead.
Pretend the link will not load on your phone browser and ask them to explain why the domain looks unusual.
Ask them to state the exact date your account was opened before discussing anything further.

scams.name: CBOB Deepfake Investment & Upfront-Fee Consumer Loan Scam
scams.name_en: Deepfake-endorsed investment platform or unlicensed fast consumer loan demanding upfront fees
scams.signals_en: Follow-up call from a deepfake investment ad misusing Bahamian leaders or a fast-loan offer demanding upfront insurance/processing fees or crypto deposits.
scams.legit_en: Central Bank of The Bahamas warns against deepfake investment ads and unlicensed consumer lenders charging advance fees.
bait_tactics: Ask for their Central Bank of The Bahamas supervised-entity details so you can look them up on the CBOB register.
Say you want the upfront loan fee deducted from the disbursed principal rather than sent separately.
Pretend you are writing down the payout schedule by hand and ask them to recalculate the monthly figures.

scams.name: Fake Job Onboarding Fee & Large Cash Prize Scam
scams.name_en: Fraudulent job advertisement or cash-prize notification requesting advance payment or bank details
scams.signals_en: Recruiter or prize agent calls/messages offering an easy high-paying job or large cash prize, asking for an upfront registration/badge fee or using the victim's personal bank account to relay funds.
scams.legit_en: Genuine Bahamian employers and regulated promotions never charge upfront hiring fees or route third-party funds through personal accounts.
bait_tactics: Ask where their physical Nassau or Freeport office is located so you can drop off paper copies in person.
Question why a legitimate company cannot pay its own administrative fee directly.
Pretend your connection is breaking up whenever payment instructions are mentioned.
